title: Own problems at staff altitude
principle: Brian Lovin’s Staff Design project (staff.design) and reflection essay: senior IC designers own ambiguous, cross-cutting problems—not only tickets. When directing AI, frame work as problem ownership with narrative and leverage, not pixel chores.
procedure: Write the problem brief: context, users, constraints, success.
Identify leverage (systems, narrative, prototypes) vs busywork.
Choose a communication artifact peers/execs can react to.
Use AI for exploration speed; keep judgment and storytelling human.
Capture what you learned for the next IC level-up.
examplePrompts:
Reframe this ticket as staff-altitude ownership (Staff Design / Lovin):
- Problem brief
- Leverage thesis
- Artifacts to create
- What AI can draft vs what I must decide
Return a one-page ownership plan.
Stop generating random screens—help me articulate the cross-team problem first.
promptWhy: Problem brief elevates above ticket farming.

workedExamples.title: Ticket tunnel
workedExamples.after: Ownership plan: alignment workshop + prototype narrative.

workedExamples.title: Leverage pick
workedExamples.body: One system fix beats twelve one-off screens.

antiPatterns: Measuring IC value only in tickets closed.
Delegating judgment entirely to the model.
